featherdrop is now CastleParcel: a new name, a new interface and a new encryption format, with every existing share still opening. Update the container to `junkerderprovinz/castleparcel`. The appdata folder keeps its old name, so `/data` and `/config` carry over untouched.

## ✨ Added

- Encrypted notes: share a piece of text instead of a file, with the same expiry, download limit, password and management link. The recipient sees it as plain text, never as rendered HTML. Paste text on the start page to begin one.
- File requests: open a request at `/request` and send its link to someone who should send you files. They upload without an account, the files are encrypted to your key in their browser, and only your private collect link can open what arrives.
- A management link next to every share link, which deletes the share and its file before it expires.
- Recipients of a limited share see the file names and sizes before they spend a download.
- A client you can check: the web client builds to the same bytes on any machine, every release carries `castleparcel-client.json` with the hash of each file, and `scripts/verify-client.mjs` compares a running instance against it. The page pins its script and stylesheet with Subresource Integrity.
- `UPLOAD_LIMIT_PER_IP` caps how many bytes one visitor can upload in 24 hours, and `TRUST_PROXY` also takes a list of proxy addresses and CIDR ranges.

## 🎨 Design

- A new interface built on the GlimStone design system, with the CastleParcel castle and sealed letter as the logo, light and dark mode, a settings page for language, theme and accent, and the same 26 languages.
- The castle loader: letters fly into the gate while you upload and back out while you download, and the tower reacts to each one. With reduced motion, a letter rests calmly at the gate instead.
- The README has its own section on the threat model: what stays private, what the operator and the network can still see, and how to check the client.

## ⚡ Improved

- Every upload writes the new encryption format. It keeps file names, sizes and the share layout inside an encrypted header, pads sizes so the server only learns a size bucket, and turns a password into a second factor next to the link, so nobody holding only the stored file can guess it offline.
- Uploads encrypt as they go, so large files need no extra copy on disk, and an upload cut off by a reload or a closed tab picks up where it stopped once you pick the same files again. Resuming needs HTTPS or localhost, because browsers only offer the crypto it relies on there.
- Encryption and decryption run in a Web Worker, so a big file no longer freezes the page. The worker ships inside the pinned script, so the integrity check covers it too.
- "Download all" saves one ZIP, built in the browser while it decrypts. On a share without a download limit, each file can still be saved on its own.
- A download counts as soon as it starts, and one that breaks off resumes without counting again. A one-time share can no longer be read by cutting the connection just before the end.
- Wrong passwords on a share are slowed down for everyone after ten misses in a row, and rate limits count failed lookups and new downloads instead of every read, so watching a video or resuming a download stays smooth.
- Uploads in progress count toward `STORAGE_QUOTA` from the moment they start, and an upload to a file request that sits idle for an hour gives its place back.
- The server sends the page's files gzipped and lets the browser keep the main script until the next release, so a visit after the first loads almost nothing.
- Strict security headers on every response, including a Content-Security-Policy that only allows the app's own scripts.

## 🐛 Fixed

- Expired shares and abandoned uploads are deleted again. The server had stopped cleaning them up, so they stayed on disk.

## 🌐 Translations

- All 26 languages are translated for the new interface, including notes, file requests and the new messages.
